messages:
sam: heads-up — we just hit a sustained eviction bump (~5%) on ap-southeast1 warm pool starting ~08:02 UTC. Scheduler logs show repeated attach/attach timeout failures and then the scheduler doing aggressive preempts due to affinity timeouts.
opsbot: [ALERT] cluster: ap-southeast1-warmpool evictions > 4% (08:05 UTC). Policy: auto-notify on sustained spike.
maria: linking grafana panel: https://grafana.internal/cluster/ap-southeast1/evictions — spike aligns with increased pod creation rate from batch-training jobs.
linh: quick question — is this strictly attach/NIC failure, or are we also seeing kubelet OOMs?
sam: it's attach-first: scheduler log snippet shows fail -> preempt loop. Seen messages like: 
```
2026-03-23T08:02:10Z scheduler: binding pod training-42 to node gpu-apse1-23 failed: attach nic timeout (conntrack watch timed out)
2026-03-23T08:02:11Z scheduler: preempting pod training-41 to free slots for training-42
```
priyanka: hmm. Recent infra change was the egress qdisc tweak on racks B/C to mitigate noisy neighbors. Could be we reduced conntrack table or bumped netfilter timeouts.
jong: I saw increased packet drops on top-of-rack for those racks earlier this morning. If attach RPCs are timing out, scheduler falls back to trying other nodes then triggers affinity-preempt churn.
rashid: immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle batch job admissions into warm pool (rate-limit) 2) bump attach RPC timeout in scheduler 3) temporarily relax strict pod anti-affinity for training jobs to spread them. Which do we want to try first?
maria: customer impact minimal, but cost/latency and node thrash are bad. Prefer non-invasive first: rate-limit admissions + revert qdisc tweak if evidence points there.
linh: to triage: can someone paste conntrack and qdisc stats from a problematic node?
sam: grabbing from gpu-apse1-23:
```
# ss -s
TCP: inuse 1232 orphan 0 tw 45 alloc 1232 mem 0
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
524288
# tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc fq_codel 0: limit 10240p drop 0 ... backlog 0
```
Seems nf_conntrack isn't exhausted but qdisc shows lots of drops on eth0.
priyanka: OK that leans qdisc. The qdisc tweak lowered fq_codel target and increased burst to help small RPCs, maybe it backfired under high fanout. Reverting to previous qdisc for a small canary could help.
jong: I'll roll qdisc revert on two racks (B/C) as canary, and set a temporary admission cap for the training job queue. Canary timeline: 2 racks now, watch 15m.
opsbot: deploybot: rolling change submitted: qdisc-revert-canary -> ap-southeast1-rack-B,C. Target: 2 nodes per rack.
sam: also opening a scheduler tweak PR to increase attach timeout from 20s -> 45s (non-breaking). Will canary that after network revert if we still see flakiness.
priyanka: spawn a small soak job that creates 200 tiny pods to reproduce attach pressure in staging with current qdisc config. If it fails, we confirm.
rashid: action items: jong -> revert qdisc on B/C and cap admissions (+ link to runbook). sam -> PR for attach timeout canary. priyanka -> run staging soak and collect tc/conntrack metrics. linH -> monitor grafana alert and set a temporary alert threshold to reduce noise.
maria: thanks — ping me when the canary shows green or if evictions go down. :thumbsup:
sam: will update in 10m.
__note: This thread is a synthetic Slack conversation for dataset purposes — messages are compact and reflect operational back-and-forth.
